subject: Fraud & Scams
title: The Social Security Suspension Scam
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Social Security Suspension Scam usable.

hook.text: A robocall says your Social Security number has been suspended. That's not a real thing.

buildup.text: The Social Security Administration doesn't suspend numbers, threaten arrest, or demand gift cards.

discovery.text: Scammers prey on fear of losing benefits that millions of Americans depend on for survival.

twist.text: This scam generates more complaints to the FTC than almost any other impersonation fraud.

climax.text: The SSA will never call and ask for your number. You gave it to them — they already have it.

punchline.text: Your Social Security number can't be suspended. Full stop.

quiz.question: Can the Social Security Administration suspend your number?
